title: Flooding normalization profile identity and its enumerable universe
description:
Standard LDPC codes in `gf2-coding` carry a canonical flooding-profile identity that represents NR rate matching exactly at bit granularity, and one library function enumerates the finite universe of table keys and default iteration caps that table generation, validation and default lookup share.

## Background

gf2's flooding LDPC decoders use normalized min-sum (NMS) with a family-wide factor of 0.75 for NR (5G) and plain min-sum for generic codes. An indication on DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at an iteration cap of 50 shows 0.75 losing more than 0.3 dB to 0.875, with AFF3CT 4.7.0 reproducing both figures, and a sample-based density-evolution (DE) estimate puts the threshold-optimal factor near 0.90 for that code, at least 0.95 for DVB-T2 short rate 1/2, 0.6 to 0.7 for NR at low and middle rates and 0.75 to 0.80 for NR at rates 0.77 to 0.88. The owner decision of @/issue/3461a52a makes the default a table of the DE-optimal factor per code profile and iteration cap, produced by an in-tree offline tool, caller-overridable, and standing only if benchmark-window curves confirm it. A profile with no table entry keeps its current behaviour: generic `LdpcDecoder::new` uses plain min-sum, and NR rate-matched constructors and explicitly selected NMS defaults keep 0.75.

NR rate matching in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/mod.rs` (`write_known_llrs`) splits base columns at bit boundaries: for BG2 `(n=256, k=121)` the constructor selects $Z=22$, with 99 filler bits and 179 kept parity bits, so both the filler start and the parity end fall inside a base column. A pattern of whole base columns cannot represent this. The profile therefore states each boundary as an exact fraction of a base column: the filler start $b_f = k/Z$ and the parity end $b_p = K_b + p/Z$, with $p$ the kept parity bits, both reduced rationals, and the number of punctured leading systematic columns (2 for rate-matched codes, 0 for the mother code). Two codes with equal reduced boundaries at different lifting sizes have one profile; protograph DE is asymptotic in the lifting size.

Table keys round $b_f$ and $b_p$ to the nearest multiple of $1/Q$ base column, with $Q$ from `de-configuration`; one key function serves generation and lookup. A DVB-T2 profile is a (frame size, code rate) pair and is its own key. `Nr5gRateMatchedCode` attaches its rate-matched profile to the mother `LdpcCode` it holds, so every backend built from `mother_code()`, the GPU decoder included, sees the rate-matched profile rather than the mother code's.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `FloodingProfile` identifies DVB-T2 (frame size, rate) profiles and NR profiles by base graph, punctured leading systematic columns, and filler-start and parity-end boundaries as reduced rationals of a base column; the standard DVB-T2 and NR constructors attach their profile to the `LdpcCode` they build, `Nr5gRateMatchedCode` attaches its rate-matched profile to its mother code, and a code built from a raw parity-check matrix carries none.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each base column's transmitted, filler and punctured fractions derive from the profile and sum to one; tests cover boundaries at a whole column, inside a column (BG2 `(256, 121)` at $Z=22$), at the first and last systematic column and at the last base column, and two codes with equal reduced boundaries at different lifting sizes map to equal profiles and equal column fractions.
- [hard] REQ-03: One function enumerates the table-key universe from the DVB-T2 code tables, the NR base-graph dimensions, `kb_for_z_selection` and the lifting sets, including unpunctured BG1 and BG2 mother profiles. Its witnesses include accepted `(base graph, n, k)` rate-matched inputs and an accepted `(base graph, lifting factor)` input for each `QuasiCyclicLdpc::nr_5g` mother constructor; tests check that every standard DVB-T2 and NR rate-matched constructor key and both mother-constructor keys are in the enumeration, and that every witness builds a code whose key matches its enumeration entry.
- [hard] REQ-04: The DVB-T2 concatenated decoder's default LDPC cap is a named public constant, and one function returns the default-cap universe from that constant and `SOFT_DECODE_MAX_ITERATIONS`.

## Notes

Decoding behaviour is unchanged: no factor is read from a profile here. The universe size is derived by the enumeration and never stated in prose.

planning.outcome: Standard LDPC codes carry a canonical flooding profile drawn from one enumerated universe

title: Density-evolution engine for flooding normalized min-sum over edge-typed ensembles
description:
`gf2-coding` computes sample-based density evolution of flooding normalized min-sum over an edge-typed ensemble and finds the threshold-optimal factor at a given iteration cap; the plain $(\lambda, \rho)$ degree distribution is its one-edge-type instance.

## Background

gf2's flooding LDPC decoders use normalized min-sum (NMS) with a family-wide factor of 0.75 for NR (5G) and plain min-sum for generic codes. An indication on DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at an iteration cap of 50 shows 0.75 losing more than 0.3 dB to 0.875, with AFF3CT 4.7.0 reproducing both figures, and a sample-based density-evolution (DE) estimate puts the threshold-optimal factor near 0.90 for that code, at least 0.95 for DVB-T2 short rate 1/2, 0.6 to 0.7 for NR at low and middle rates and 0.75 to 0.80 for NR at rates 0.77 to 0.88. The owner decision of @/issue/3461a52a makes the default a table of the DE-optimal factor per code profile and iteration cap, produced by an in-tree offline tool, caller-overridable, and standing only if benchmark-window curves confirm it. A profile with no table entry keeps its current behaviour: generic `LdpcDecoder::new` uses plain min-sum, and NR rate-matched constructors and explicitly selected NMS defaults keep 0.75.

Zhang, Fossorier, Gu and Zhang (GLOBECOM 2005, doi:10.1109/glocom.2005.1577841) choose the factor that minimizes the DE threshold; Emran and Elsabrouty (arXiv:1501.07336) apply it to DVB codes; Chen and Fossorier (IEEE Commun. Lett. 2002, doi:10.1109/4234.1001666) originate the method. The DVB-T2 staircase ensemble and the NR protograph ensemble are later instances of the same engine, so the engine's ensemble carries edge types, variable types with a channel input that mixes Gaussian, erased and known values with given weights, and check types. Under `@/inv/library-first-generality` the DE mathematics is a library API; search orchestration and generation stay in a tool.

The validation section of [findings-b8157e14.md](findings-b8157e14.md) gives an exact discrete DE threshold of 1.212 dB for the regular (3,6) ensemble at NMS 0.75, flooding, cap 200, target bit error probability $10^{-4}$, an in-repository estimate this engine is checked against.

Every DE computation declares its seed, sample count, factor grid, threshold precision, stopping rule and iteration cap. The fixed configuration of `de-configuration` uses seed 3461, a factor grid no coarser than 0.025 over $[0.5, 1.0]$, threshold bisection that stops at 0.05 dB for DVB-T2 and 0.1 dB for NR, over BPSK AWGN with the all-zero codeword.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: For a declared configuration, the API returns the DE threshold of an edge-typed ensemble at a factor and cap, and the threshold-optimal factor over the factor grid; identical inputs produce identical output.
- [hard] REQ-02: The $(\lambda, \rho)$ instance of a regular (3,6) ensemble at NMS 0.75, cap 200 and target $10^{-4}$ lies within the declared DVB-T2 precision of 1.212 dB.
- [hard] REQ-03: A variable type whose channel input is fully erased or fully known behaves as a punctured or a known node: tests on small ensembles check the limiting densities.
- [hard] REQ-04: Fast-tier tests use small sample counts within the per-test budget; the (3,6) threshold check runs as a descriptive slow-tier test, and the module is registered in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/mod.rs`.

planning.outcome: Flooding NMS density evolution over edge-typed ensembles is a deterministic gf2-coding API

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One numerical module with its threshold search and the one-edge-type instance fits one focused cycle.

title: Two-edge-type staircase density evolution for DVB-T2 profiles
description:
`gf2-coding` builds the two-edge-type staircase ensemble of a DVB-T2 profile from its code table and evaluates it with the density-evolution engine, so a DVB-T2 profile's factor derives from its information and staircase parity structure.

## Background

gf2's flooding LDPC decoders use normalized min-sum (NMS) with a family-wide factor of 0.75 for NR (5G) and plain min-sum for generic codes. An indication on DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at an iteration cap of 50 shows 0.75 losing more than 0.3 dB to 0.875, with AFF3CT 4.7.0 reproducing both figures, and a sample-based density-evolution (DE) estimate puts the threshold-optimal factor near 0.90 for that code, at least 0.95 for DVB-T2 short rate 1/2, 0.6 to 0.7 for NR at low and middle rates and 0.75 to 0.80 for NR at rates 0.77 to 0.88. The owner decision of @/issue/3461a52a makes the default a table of the DE-optimal factor per code profile and iteration cap, produced by an in-tree offline tool, caller-overridable, and standing only if benchmark-window curves confirm it. A profile with no table entry keeps its current behaviour: generic `LdpcDecoder::new` uses plain min-sum, and NR rate-matched constructors and explicitly selected NMS defaults keep 0.75.

Under the plain $(\lambda, \rho)$ ensemble the degree-2 subgraph of a DVB-T2 code branches ($\lambda_2 \rho'(1) = 1.71 > 1$ for normal rate 1/2), while the IRA staircase makes it a path. The validation section of [findings-b8157e14.md](findings-b8157e14.md) shows the plain model agreeing at cap 50 and differing by 0.09 dB at cap 200 for DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at NMS 0.875, with a spurious fixed point near the $10^{-4}$ target. The two-edge-type ensemble has information edges from the table's information columns and staircase edges on the degree-2 parity columns; each check's information and staircase edge counts come from the table. As in those findings, the single degree-1 parity column and the parity wrap are ignored.

Zhang et al. report 0.75 as the optimal single factor for the (16200, 7200) code with a 0.90 dB threshold; the estimate of @/issue/3461a52a gives at least 0.95 and 2.72 dB at 0.75 under the plain model, and Emran and Elsabrouty report 0.9375. The ensemble lives with the DVB-T2 code tables in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/dvb_t2/`.

Every DE computation declares its seed, sample count, factor grid, threshold precision, stopping rule and iteration cap. The fixed configuration of `de-configuration` uses seed 3461, a factor grid no coarser than 0.025 over $[0.5, 1.0]$, threshold bisection that stops at 0.05 dB for DVB-T2 and 0.1 dB for NR, over BPSK AWGN with the all-zero codeword.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: For every DVB-T2 profile the ensemble's per-type variable degrees and check edge counts derive from its code table, and its information and staircase edge counts match the parity-check matrix of the built `LdpcCode` less the ignored degree-1 column.
- [hard] REQ-02: An ensemble without staircase edges reduces to the engine's $(\lambda, \rho)$ instance and gives identical output under the same configuration.
- [hard] REQ-03: Slow-tier tests with descriptive ignores compute DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at NMS 0.875 at caps 50 and 200 under both ensembles, and recompute the Zhang et al. (16200, 7200) factor and threshold under both; each outcome is recorded in @/issue/3461a52a with source and configuration, and a contradiction with a cited figure is recorded as a falsification.
- [hard] REQ-04: Fast-tier tests use small sample counts within the per-test budget.

planning.outcome: DVB-T2 profiles have a staircase-aware two-edge-type density-evolution ensemble

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One ensemble builder over the DVB-T2 tables with its numerical checks is one focused cycle on an existing engine.

title: Protograph density evolution with fractional base-column transmission
description:
`gf2-coding` builds the protograph ensemble of an NR profile from its base graph and exact column fractions and evaluates it with the density-evolution engine, so an NR profile's factor derives from its base graph and bit-granular transmission pattern.

## Background

gf2's flooding LDPC decoders use normalized min-sum (NMS) with a family-wide factor of 0.75 for NR (5G) and plain min-sum for generic codes. An indication on DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at an iteration cap of 50 shows 0.75 losing more than 0.3 dB to 0.875, with AFF3CT 4.7.0 reproducing both figures, and a sample-based density-evolution (DE) estimate puts the threshold-optimal factor near 0.90 for that code, at least 0.95 for DVB-T2 short rate 1/2, 0.6 to 0.7 for NR at low and middle rates and 0.75 to 0.80 for NR at rates 0.77 to 0.88. The owner decision of @/issue/3461a52a makes the default a table of the DE-optimal factor per code profile and iteration cap, produced by an in-tree offline tool, caller-overridable, and standing only if benchmark-window curves confirm it. A profile with no table entry keeps its current behaviour: generic `LdpcDecoder::new` uses plain min-sum, and NR rate-matched constructors and explicitly selected NMS defaults keep 0.75.

Each base column is a variable type whose channel input mixes transmitted (Gaussian), filler (known) and punctured or untransmitted (erased) values with the column's fractions from `FloodingProfile`; each base row is a check type; each base edge is an edge type. Under random lifting this mixture is exact in the lifting limit, so a boundary inside a column needs no rounding. The base graphs are `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/bg1.rs` and `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/bg2.rs`; the ensemble lives with them in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/`. The optimum depends on rate and iteration cap.

Every DE computation declares its seed, sample count, factor grid, threshold precision, stopping rule and iteration cap. The fixed configuration of `de-configuration` uses seed 3461, a factor grid no coarser than 0.025 over $[0.5, 1.0]$, threshold bisection that stops at 0.05 dB for DVB-T2 and 0.1 dB for NR, over BPSK AWGN with the all-zero codeword.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: For every NR profile, including the BG1 and BG2 unpunctured mother profiles, and cap, the API returns the protograph DE threshold at a factor and the threshold-optimal factor over the factor grid, with each column's channel input weighted by its fractions; identical inputs produce identical output.
- [hard] REQ-02: Profiles with equal reduced boundaries built at different lifting sizes give identical output; a boundary at a whole column gives the same output as the whole-column state; tests include a boundary inside a column.
- [hard] REQ-03: A regular protograph whose lifted ensemble equals an unstructured degree distribution gives the same threshold as the engine's $(\lambda, \rho)$ instance within declared precision.
- [hard] REQ-04: Fast-tier tests stay within the per-test budget; full base-graph runs are slow-tier tests with a descriptive ignore.

planning.outcome: Flooding NMS protograph density evolution covers NR profiles at bit-granular boundaries

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One protograph ensemble builder with fractional channel inputs on an existing engine is one focused cycle.

title: Offline density-evolution tool and the committed flooding factor table
description:
An offline executable `ldpc-density-evolution` computes the DE-optimal flooding factor for one profile and cap and regenerates the committed `FLOODING_NMS_FACTORS` table in `gf2-coding` over the library's enumerated (profile, cap) universe, so the table is reproducible from one command and one fixed configuration.

## Background

gf2's flooding LDPC decoders use normalized min-sum (NMS) with a family-wide factor of 0.75 for NR (5G) and plain min-sum for generic codes. An indication on DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at an iteration cap of 50 shows 0.75 losing more than 0.3 dB to 0.875, with AFF3CT 4.7.0 reproducing both figures, and a sample-based density-evolution (DE) estimate puts the threshold-optimal factor near 0.90 for that code, at least 0.95 for DVB-T2 short rate 1/2, 0.6 to 0.7 for NR at low and middle rates and 0.75 to 0.80 for NR at rates 0.77 to 0.88. The owner decision of @/issue/3461a52a makes the default a table of the DE-optimal factor per code profile and iteration cap, produced by an in-tree offline tool, caller-overridable, and standing only if benchmark-window curves confirm it. A profile with no table entry keeps its current behaviour: generic `LdpcDecoder::new` uses plain min-sum, and NR rate-matched constructors and explicitly selected NMS defaults keep 0.75.

The tool is a workspace member under `dev/tools/`, like `dev/tools/tuning-campaign-support`. It depends on `gf2-coding` for the profile universe and the DE APIs and holds only CLI, search orchestration and source generation, under `@/inv/library-first-generality` and `@/inv/crate-dependency-direction`; no production crate depends on it. The generated table is a Rust source file in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/`, keyed by `FloodingProfile` and iteration cap. It is derived library configuration under `@/inv/structural-performance-defaults`: each entry follows from a code's structure and cap, not from a host measurement. Raw DE samples stay outside the tree under `@/inv/committed-evidence-budget`.

DVB-T2 entries use the staircase ensemble and NR entries the protograph ensemble at the table key's boundaries; the tool adds no numerical model.

Every DE computation declares its seed, sample count, factor grid, threshold precision, stopping rule and iteration cap. The fixed configuration uses seed 3461, a factor grid no coarser than 0.025 over $[0.5, 1.0]$, threshold bisection that stops at 0.05 dB for DVB-T2 and 0.1 dB for NR, over BPSK AWGN with the all-zero codeword, and NR key resolution $Q = 4$.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A `compute` command prints the threshold-optimal factor and its threshold for one named profile and cap under the fixed configuration.
- [hard] REQ-02: A `regenerate` command writes the table source for every (table key, cap) pair the library enumerates, including both BG1 and BG2 mother keys, takes the universe from the library rather than a list of its own, and records the configuration in the generated file's header; the mother entries are generated before validation consumes the table, and two runs with the same configuration write byte-identical output, checked on a reduced universe in a fast-tier test.
- [hard] REQ-03: The committed table has exactly one entry per enumerated (table key, cap) pair, including the BG1 and BG2 mother entries, checked by a fast-tier test against the enumeration, and no decoder default reads it.
- [hard] REQ-04: Each committed entry that departs from the recorded DE estimate ranges, and the outcome for the DVB-T2 short rate 1/2 falsification candidate, is recorded in @/issue/3461a52a with the configuration.
- [hard] REQ-05: DVB-T2 entries come from the `dvb-t2-staircase-de` ensemble and NR entries from the `protograph-de` ensemble at each key's boundaries; the tool holds no density-evolution mathematics of its own.

planning.outcome: One offline command regenerates the committed flooding factor table from the universe

terminal.worker_sized_reason: A thin CLI over the two library ensembles and the engine, run once to commit its output, is one focused cycle.

title: Window-curve harness for the flooding normalization table
description:
An experiment harness measures FER curves for sampled flooding profiles at the pre-registered candidate factors and applies the pre-registered decision rule, so the window campaigns confirm or falsify table entries mechanically.

## Background

gf2's flooding LDPC decoders use normalized min-sum (NMS) with a family-wide factor of 0.75 for NR (5G) and plain min-sum for generic codes. An indication on DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at an iteration cap of 50 shows 0.75 losing more than 0.3 dB to 0.875, with AFF3CT 4.7.0 reproducing both figures, and a sample-based density-evolution (DE) estimate puts the threshold-optimal factor near 0.90 for that code, at least 0.95 for DVB-T2 short rate 1/2, 0.6 to 0.7 for NR at low and middle rates and 0.75 to 0.80 for NR at rates 0.77 to 0.88. The owner decision of @/issue/3461a52a makes the default a table of the DE-optimal factor per code profile and iteration cap, produced by an in-tree offline tool, caller-overridable, and standing only if benchmark-window curves confirm it. A profile with no table entry keeps its current behaviour: generic `LdpcDecoder::new` uses plain min-sum, and NR rate-matched constructors and explicitly selected NMS defaults keep 0.75.

The pre-registered decision rule is fixed before any measurement. Sample: every DVB-T2 (frame size, rate) profile, and per NR base graph the mother code plus the rate-matched profiles at the lowest, median and highest rate of the enumerated universe, plus one rate-matched profile whose exact boundaries lie off the key grid, each at its library default cap. Candidates per entry: the table factor $\alpha^*$, $\alpha^* \pm 0.05$, 0.75, plain min-sum where it is the current default and, for DVB-T2, the layered configuration's 0.875, intersected with the decoder's factor domain $(0, 1]$ of `DecoderConfig::new` and deduplicated by factor, with plain min-sum counted as factor 1.0. Each FER point runs until 100 frame errors or 200 000 frames over BPSK AWGN with seed 3461, random codewords and syndrome stopping; the FER $10^{-3}$ crossing is log-linear interpolation between the bracketing points of a 0.05 dB grid, with an interval from 95% Wilson bounds on those points. An entry is confirmed when the crossing of $\alpha^*$ lies within 0.05 dB of the best candidate's crossing; falsified when a candidate's crossing is better by more than 0.05 dB with non-overlapping intervals; otherwise unconfirmed. The rule stands for a family when every sampled entry is confirmed. A falsified entry is recorded, regenerated with its DE configuration corrected and measured once more; a second falsification rejects the rule for that family. 

The harness lives under `experiments/` and consumes `gf2-coding` and `experiments/common` for run identity and durable publication, under `@/inv/convention-convergence`. It is a campaign under `@/inv/campaign-evidence`: resumable bounded runs, one append-only execution log outside the tracked tree, and a record pinning executable digest, configuration, seed and observed host facts.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The committed configuration states the sample, candidates, stopping rule, seed, grid, crossing estimator, interval and tolerance of the rule above, and the harness takes the sample from the library's profile enumeration, including both BG1 and BG2 mother profiles; their table entries are generated before validation runs.
- [hard] REQ-02: For each sampled entry the harness reports per-candidate crossings with intervals and the entry verdict (confirmed, falsified or unconfirmed); a fast-tier test checks the verdict logic on synthetic curves at the tolerance boundary.
- [hard] REQ-03: A run resumes from its execution log without repeating completed points, and identical seed and configuration give identical counts across worker counts.
- [hard] REQ-04: Each run names harness, configuration, iteration cap and host, and labels runs outside the benchmark window as indications.
- [hard] REQ-05: Unit tests of the candidate set cover $\alpha^* = 1.0$, where $\alpha^* + 0.05$ is dropped and plain min-sum coincides with $\alpha^*$, $\alpha^* = 0.975$, and an interior optimum; every candidate is accepted by `DecoderConfig::new` and none repeats.

planning.outcome: A resumable harness applies the pre-registered rule to sampled flooding profiles

terminal.test_boundary: harness unit tests on synthetic curves
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One experiment crate reusing the shared run mechanics fits one focused cycle.

title: Shared flooding normalization policy over the factor table
description:
One caller-overridable `gf2-coding` policy resolves the flooding normalization of every decode path, scalar, batch and GPU, from the code's flooding profile and the actual iteration cap through `FLOODING_NMS_FACTORS`.

## Background

gf2's flooding LDPC decoders use normalized min-sum (NMS) with a family-wide factor of 0.75 for NR (5G) and plain min-sum for generic codes. An indication on DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at an iteration cap of 50 shows 0.75 losing more than 0.3 dB to 0.875, with AFF3CT 4.7.0 reproducing both figures, and a sample-based density-evolution (DE) estimate puts the threshold-optimal factor near 0.90 for that code, at least 0.95 for DVB-T2 short rate 1/2, 0.6 to 0.7 for NR at low and middle rates and 0.75 to 0.80 for NR at rates 0.77 to 0.88. The owner decision of @/issue/3461a52a makes the default a table of the DE-optimal factor per code profile and iteration cap, produced by an in-tree offline tool, caller-overridable, and standing only if benchmark-window curves confirm it. A profile with no table entry keeps its current behaviour: generic `LdpcDecoder::new` uses plain min-sum, and NR rate-matched constructors and explicitly selected NMS defaults keep 0.75.

Every scalar flooding decode reaches `LdpcDecoder::decode_codeword_into` in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/core.rs`: `decode_iterative` and `decode_to_codeword` call it, `Nr5gRateMatchedDecoder` reaches it through `decode_to_codeword` on the mother-code decoder (`crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/mod.rs`), and so does the concatenated DVB-T2 decoder (`crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/dvb_t2/concat.rs`). The cap is an argument of that entry, so scalar resolution happens there, memoized per cap. Batch and GPU backends receive their cap at construction: `LdpcBatchDecoder::new` and `with_selectors` in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/batch.rs`, and the GPU configuration entry `GpuLdpcBp::new` in `crates/gf2-sim/src/gpu/ldpc_bp.rs`, which creates the CPU fallback through `CpuLdpcBp::new`; selector-specific fallback construction is `CpuLdpcBp::with_selectors` in that module. The GPU kernel and CPU fallback use the same resolved configuration; `GpuNr5gDecoder` in `crates/gf2-sim/src/gpu/nr_5g_ldpc.rs` builds `GpuLdpcBp` from `mother_code()`, which carries the rate-matched profile. The checkpoint identity in `crates/gf2-sim/src/snr_checkpoint.rs` hashes `DecoderConfig::algorithm()`.

`DecoderConfig` therefore holds a check-rule request, an explicit `DecoderAlgorithm` or `CodeDefault { fallback: DecoderAlgorithm }`; the default request carries the current constructor's fallback. Generic `LdpcDecoder::new` uses `DecoderAlgorithm::MinSum`, while the NR rate-matched wrapper uses `DecoderAlgorithm::NormalizedMinSum(0.75)`. One function resolves a request with an optional profile and a cap to a resolved configuration; an explicit request wins, and a request without a table entry, or for a family whose validation has not confirmed the rule, resolves to its fallback payload. Resolution is behaviour-preserving when it lands, because no family is enabled yet. Backends, kernel mapping, CPU fallbacks and checkpoint identity read only resolved configurations, so the CPU fallback and the GPU kernel decode with one factor and a checkpoint records the factor that ran. Existing readers of `DecoderConfig::algorithm()` move to the request or the resolved form in this change, and the old accessor is removed under `@/inv/canonical-cutover`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Failing behavioural tests precede the implementation and cover explicit precedence, the actual cap at the scalar entry, the cap at batch and GPU construction, absent entries, families not yet enabled, and an NR rate-matched code resolving by its rate-matched profile on every path; an uncovered cap returns the `MinSum` fallback from generic `LdpcDecoder::new` and the `NormalizedMinSum(0.75)` fallback from the NR wrapper.
- [hard] REQ-02: A code-default decode produces the same decisions and iteration counts as the same decode with the resolved factor passed explicitly, across the scalar, SIMD, batch and GPU flooding backends' shared conformance suite, and the GPU stage and its CPU fallback resolve to the same algorithm.
- [hard] REQ-03: The suite checks that the checkpoint identity of a code-default configuration equals that of the explicitly resolved configuration it runs.
- [hard] REQ-04: The policy's rustdoc states the precedence, the absent-entry behaviour and the per-family enablement, and cites the table as the single source of factors.

## Notes

No family is enabled here; the adoption leaves enable DVB-T2 and NR after their validations.

planning.outcome: Scalar, batch and GPU flooding decodes resolve their factor through one caller-overridable policy

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One configuration type change landed with its mechanical reader migration, so the workspace builds at every commit, is one focused cycle.

footprint.uncertainty: The remaining readers of `DecoderConfig::algorithm()` in tests and experiments, and the shared backend conformance suite the policy joins, are located by the worker from the compiler and the existing LDPC contract tests.
